blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 2 killings of trans women and people of a locally established trans-feminine identity in 2025. Against a population of ~3.3 million the rate is approximately 0.61 per million per year, above the national average but below the cluster formed by three adjacent states/provinces with the country's highest such rates. This state/province belongs to a bloc of neighbouring states/provinces that absorbed 38 of 80 national killings in 2025, so it sits in a region of elevated violence even though its own absolute count is modest.

The above-national rate and regional concentration justify a small deviation below the national average. Compared with a neighbouring state/province that recorded 4 killings on a similar population (rate ~1.0 per million), this state/province is materially less severe, and the small absolute number (2) means a single case would shift the rate dramatically. No unit-specific legal restriction or enforcement finding was identified.
